title: Base change and fpqc descent of dimension-filtered module flatness
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $f:X\to Y$ have scheme base $Y$, be locally of finite type, and let $M$ be a finite type quasi-coherent module. For a scheme $B\to Y$, write $X_B=X\times_YB$ and $M_B$ for tensor pullback. For an integer $n\geq0$, let $P_n(X,M;B)$ mean that for every representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_B$ and $u\in U$ mapping to $v\in B$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\geq n$, the stalk $(a^*M_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,v}$. Residue fields, transcendence degree and base-flatness are [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. The condition $P_n$ is preserved by every scheme base change $B\prime\to B$. For every fpqc covering $\{B_i\to B\}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], $P_n(X,M;B)$ holds if and only if $P_n(X,M;B_i)$ holds for all $i$. Moreover $P_n(X,M;B)$ is equivalent to the same stalk criterion on any one representable surjective etale scheme atlas of $X_B$. Thus the assignments $B\mapsto\{b:B\to Y\mid P_n(X,M;B)\}$, with restriction by composition, form an fpqc sheaf of sets over $Y$.

proof.text: Fix a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$. For any $B\to Y$, its pullback $U_B\to X_B$ is again such an atlas. Compare a point $w$ of any chart $W\to X_B$ with a lift $u$ on $U_B$: the scheme $W\times_{X_B}U_B\to W$ is surjective etale, so choose $z$ above $w$ and let $u$ be its other image. The two etale projections give finite separable extensions $\kappa(z)/\kappa(w)$ and $\kappa(z)/\kappa(u)$. The transcendence-degree tower equality therefore gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(w)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(z)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u)$, where $b$ is their common image in $B$. Pointwise module flatness is independent of these chart choices by the cited point-chart lemma. Thus the cutoff criterion on $U_B$ implies it on every chart; the reverse implication follows by taking that chart. This proves the asserted one-atlas equivalence, also for any other atlas.

source.place: Tag 0CWS (lemma-pre-flat-dimension-n), equivalence of (1) and (2); chart comparison spelled out using Tag 04NK.

proof.text: On the fixed atlas, let $F$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent module corresponding to $p^*M$. The Zariski/etale equivalence identifies all its scheme tensor pullbacks with the chart pullbacks of $M$. In particular repeated pullbacks agree: the map $(r\otimes m)\otimes s\mapsto rs\otimes m$ and its inverse $s\otimes m\mapsto(1\otimes m)\otimes s$ give the tensor associativity identifications. The map $U\to Y$ is locally finite type by the chart hypothesis. This remains so on $U_B\to B$: on affine presentations a finite generating set of an $A$-algebra $C$ also generates $C\otimes_A A\prime$ over $A\prime$. A finite list of module generators likewise pulls back to generators. Consequently the locally finite type hypothesis needed for the residue-transcendence lemma holds at every subsequent scheme base change of this atlas.

source.place: Tags 0CWS and 0CWT; scheme reduction and the base-change construction in situation-flat-dimension-n.

proof.text: Assume $P_n(X,M;B)$ and take $B\prime\to B$. For $u\prime\in U_{B\prime}$ over $b\prime$ with residue transcendence degree at least $n$, let $u\in U_B$ and $b\in B$ be its images. The base-change inequality gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u)\geq\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b\prime)}\kappa(u\prime)\geq n$. Hence $(F_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. Clause (1) of pointwise module flatness under base change makes $(F_{B\prime})_{u\prime}$ flat over $\mathcal O_{B\prime,b\prime}$. Step 1 now gives $P_n(X,M;B\prime)$.

source.place: Tag 0CWS, final assertion; scheme pointwise argument using Tag 02FY (2) and Tag 047C (1).

proof.text: Let $\{B_i\to B\}$ be fpqc and assume $P_n(X,M;B_i)$ for every $i$. Given $u\in U_B$ over $b$ of residue transcendence degree at least $n$, choose $i$ and $b_i\in B_i$ above $b$ using the covering condition. The equality-lift clause gives $u_i\in U_B\times_B B_i=U_{B_i}$ over $u,b_i$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b_i)}\kappa(u_i)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u)\geq n$. By hypothesis $(F_{B_i})_{u_i}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B_i,b_i}$. The map $B_i\to B$ is flat, so clause (2) of pointwise module flatness under base change implies that $(F_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. Step 1 gives $P_n(X,M;B)$. The other direction is step 3 applied to each $B_i\to B$.

source.place: Tag 0CWW (lemma-flat-dimension-n), part (1); direct pointwise form of the proof of scheme Tag 05MV, using Tag 02FY (3).

proof.text: Step 3 defines restrictions by composition and the tensor associativity in step 2 gives their identity and composition laws. For compatible local sections $b_i:B_i\to Y$ over an fpqc covering of a test scheme $B$, representable fpqc descent gives a unique morphism $b:B\to Y$ restricting to them. Apply step 4 to this morphism and the given covering: since each $b_i$ satisfies the cutoff condition, so does $b$. Uniqueness of $b$ proves uniqueness of the glued section. On the relative site of schemes over $Y$ the values are simply singleton or empty and the same argument proves the sheaf assertion there. For the empty test scheme the criterion is vacuous and the unique empty morphism is the unique section.

source.place: Tag 0CWW (lemma-flat-dimension-n), part (1), with the interpretation of F_n as a subfunctor of Y immediately before it.
